channel.title: PK INDUSTRIES - Steel Plant Consumables Blog
channel.description: Practical technical articles on casting powder, nozzle filling compound, refractory castable, mortar and ladle covering compound.

item.title: Running a Monthly Free-Opening Audit and Acting on the Number
item.description: Free opening is the one ladle number worth tracking every month. How to count it honestly, what the pattern means, and what to change first.

item.title: Getting a Reliable First Read from a Disposable Thermocouple Tip
item.description: A failed read costs a repeat immersion and a stale number. Immersion practice, lance condition, and judging a batch across a shift.

item.title: Receiving and Inspecting a Consumables Delivery Before It Reaches the Floor
item.description: The cheapest quality control a shop has is fifteen minutes at the gate. What to check on arrival, and why a problem found later is untraceable.

item.title: Why a Ladle Does Not Open Freely, and What to Check First
item.description: Free opening rate is one of the cleanest indicators of ladle practice health. Here are the four causes behind most failures, and the order to check them in.

item.title: Applying Ladle Covering Compound: Timing, Coverage and Topping Up
item.description: Ladle covering compound only saves temperature if the layer is unbroken. When to add it, how to judge coverage, and when topping up stops helping.

item.title: The First Heat-Up of a Refractory Castable, and Why Rushing It Spalls the Lining
item.description: Explosive spalling on first fire is a water problem, not a material problem. What happens inside the lining, and how to build a heat-up schedule.

item.title: Filling the Ladle Nozzle, Step by Step
item.description: A repeatable filling procedure for the ladle well and nozzle, why the sequence matters more than the quantity, and the shortcuts that cost you a free open.

item.title: Storing and Handling Nozzle Filling Compound Without Losing Free Opening
item.description: Most free opening losses are decided in the store, not at the ladle. A practical storage and handling procedure, and the three habits that quietly undo it.

item.title: Mixing Refractory Mortar and Getting Joint Thickness Right
item.description: Most joint failures start at the mixing board. Water control, consistency, joint thickness, and the shortcuts that undo all three.

item.title: Casting Powder Feeding Practice and Controlling Slag Pool Depth
item.description: Consumption per tonne is an outcome, not a setting. How feeding practice determines slag pool depth, and the habits that quietly wreck both.
